context: Request: top five clients by number of matters, with counts (relationship review). Rubric: client prefixes 1038 Cascade Retail, 1008 Lumos, 1025 Quorum at 10 matters each; 1016 Dunmore, 1017 Aurelius, 1018 Penterra tied at 9 at the cutoff; all six reported with counts and the tie explained. No matter numbers named.

declared: List files in the document store (attempt 3). Saves the folder list, counts folders and the folders with an engagement file, and names the two without one.

stages.note: Reads the opening lines of three engagement letters from different number prefixes; two reads on folder paths fail.
Counts matters per number prefix from the saved folder list; three prefixes at ten and three at nine.

stages.note: Extraction of engagement-letter openings for every matter in the six leading prefixes (heredoc error, then a run saved to a file).

stages.stage: Read a chosen matter's documents in depth
stages.note: Lists one matter without an engagement file and reads four of its documents to name its client.

stages.stage: Read a chosen matter's documents in depth

Writes the ranking with the three-way tie at the cutoff, six clients with their matter lists and sources.
Re-reads the response; a count script fails on the workspace path and reruns against the output folder.
Attempt 2: reads one engagement letter per ranked client and recounts per prefix.
Attempt 3: direct recount of folders and a re-read of the response opening.
Attempt 4: reads the openings of seven client documents and four continuations; the review says keep the response.
Calls finish.

divergence: All pass with the same procedure: after the capped glob, a full folder enumeration, a per-prefix matter count (three prefixes at ten, three at nine), and engagement-letter reads or extraction scans to name the client behind each leading prefix and resolve matters without an engagement letter; the answer reports all six with the tie at the cutoff. Reviews repeatedly flagged that prefix counts were treated as client counts; each run answered by reading more client documents rather than changing the count.
